title: fix(plugin-sharing)!: a manual share or sharing rule to a user id that names no user is refused instead of stored as an inert grant
body:
Fixes #33912

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: none — no published skill describes the shares or sharing-rules request body; the declared `sharingRules` metadata path is not judged by this change

## 维护者速读

- 管理员或记录所有者在共享记录、保存共享规则时,若填写的用户不存在(或在多组织部署下不属于该组织),现在会立即收到错误提示,不再假装共享成功。
- 为什么做:之前这类共享看起来已授权、实际谁也访问不到,属于"看似生效、其实无效"的授权问题,替记录共享的使用者解决。
- 出错会怎样:填写正确用户的共享与规则不受影响;已存的旧共享不会被改动;如有误拒,撤回本改动即可恢复原行为。
- 要你做什么:无。

## What changes

- `SharingService.grant` (non-system path) now asks whether a `user` recipient names a user the read and write gates could ever match, after authorization, after the record's organization is resolved and after both ADR-0111 D7 halves:
  - walled posture (`isolated` / `group`) with the record's organization known: a member of that organization (objectql `organizationMemberStanding`, the engine's one membership predicate; a banned member still resolves);
  - otherwise (`single`, a record with no organization, or no membership table): an existing `sys_user`;
  - a deployment that registers no `sys_user` has nothing to resolve against and the check stands aside.
- A recipient that does not resolve is refused `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400 at the REST door) and nothing is written. A user of another organization gets the same sentence as an id that does not exist (only the echoed id differs), so the door is no cross-tenant existence oracle.
- `SharingRuleService.defineRule` applies the same check, in the rule's organization, to a non-system `user` recipient only when the rule is new or its recipient changes; re-saving a stored rule with its recipient unchanged (for example `active: false`) is not re-judged.
- The system context (rule materialisation) is unchanged.
- Kept from the predecessor's WIP (`ee1dabfcd`, seat 7), with two corrections: the direct-grant check moved from inside the non-system branch to after `assertRecipientNotInert`, so the D7 inertness verdict stays one answer per object and recipient population whoever calls (the WIP turned the user-path answer on a public object into `VALIDATION_FAILED` while the system path answered `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED`, red in `system-caller-inert-grant.test.ts`); and the "is this a direct grant" decision is a local flag set in the existing branch rather than a second `isSystem` read in `grant` (`check:system-context-census` register).
- ADR-0087 semantic ledger entry `share-user-recipient-unresolved-refused` (step 19), two changesets (plugin-sharing `minor`, spec `patch`), and a docs note in `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`.

Files to read first, by risk:

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` — the `userRecipientRefusal` / `userRecipientResolves` pair and the hunk after `assertRecipientNotInert` in `grant()` (ordering is the load-bearing part).
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts` — the `defineRule` hunk: which upserts are judged.
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/record-share-unknown-recipient.test.ts` — the pins.

## Tests

New `record-share-unknown-recipient.test.ts`, on a real ObjectQL engine over an in-memory SQLite `SqlDriver` with `sys_user` and `sys_member` registered. Refusals assert the `code` (the `CODE:` prefix the share and rule routes map to a status, `VALIDATION_FAILED` to 400, pinned route-side in `rest-share-refusal-classification.test.ts`), the exact sentence and the table left empty; the status is measured at the live door below.

- walled: unknown id refused, no row; member CONTROL granted; another-organization user answered identically to an unknown id; system context still writes the grant;
- single: unknown id refused, no row; existing user CONTROL granted with no membership asked;
- `defineRule`: unknown user refused, no rule; another-organization user identical to unknown; member CONTROL stored; an unchanged stored recipient not re-judged (`active: false` lands); moving a stored rule onto an unknown user refused.

`system-caller-inert-grant.test.ts`: the #25549 fixture's members are now also `sys_user` rows (every member is a user).

Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each leg restored to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty): each mutation reds exactly the pins it should and no control.

<details><summary>Ablation readings</summary>

| Mutation | Red |
|:--|:--|
| A1 `grant` check replaced by `null` | 3 of 11 (walled unknown, walled other-org, single unknown) |
| A2 `defineRule` check replaced by `null` | 3 of 11 (rule unknown, rule other-org, rule moved) |
| A3 membership arm disabled (`if (false)`) | 2 of 11 (both other-org cases) |
| A4 "recipient unchanged" condition deleted | 1 of 11 (unchanged stored rule re-judged) |
| A5 direct-grant flag forced `true` | 1 of 11 (system context judged) |

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, not touched: `rule-hooks.ts` binds no `user`-recipient guard on `sys_sharing_rule`, so a rule row saved through the `/data` door (the Setup form) skips the new `defineRule` check (the predecessor's finding; source read, not measured live). Reported to the seat.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/federated-phantom-share-grant.dogfood.test.ts` shares a local note with `usr_grantee_8119`, a user id that does not exist, and asserts only "not 422 / not SHARING_NOT_ENABLED"; it now passes on a 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` instead of a 201. Still green, but no longer for the reason it was written; outside this card's file surface, left as is.
- `POST /api/v1/sharing/rules` answers its refusals in the older flat `{ code, error }` body (pre-existing, unchanged here), the shares route in the nested `{ success, error: { code, message } }` envelope.
- Shares and rules already stored are not rewritten; the ledger entry tells an upgrading operator how to find inert rows.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/record-share-unknown-recipient.test.ts` — expect 11 passed.
